title: Rectangle discrepancy bound for the inner product
statement:
Fix a natural number $n$ and equip the set $\{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n$ of pairs of $n$-bit Boolean vectors with the uniform probability measure. Let $\mathrm{IP}_n(x,y) = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}(x_i \wedge y_i)$ be the mod-2 inner product. Then for every rectangle $R \subseteq \{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n$ — that is, every set of the form $R = A \times B$ with $A, B \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ — the discrepancy of $\mathrm{IP}_n$ on $R$ satisfies
\[
  \bigl|\mathrm{disc}(\mathrm{IP}_n, R)\bigr|
  \;\le\;
  \sqrt{\frac{1}{2^{n}}},
\]
where the discrepancy is the expectation over a uniformly random pair $(x,y)$ of $\mathbf{1}_R(x,y)\,\sigma(\mathrm{IP}_n(x,y))$, with $\sigma$ the sign map sending $\mathrm{false} \mapsto 1$ and $\mathrm{true} \mapsto -1$.
hypotheses_covered: n a natural number (the bit length)
R is a rectangle, i.e. R = A × B for some A, B ⊆ {0,1}^n
discrepancy taken with respect to the uniform finite probability measure on the pair space
replaced:
Every combinatorial rectangle $R \subseteq \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n \times \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$
has discrepancy at most $2^{-n/2}$ for the mod-2 inner product function under the
uniform distribution:
\[
  \bigl|\mathrm{disc}(\mathrm{IP}_n, R)\bigr|
  \;\le\; \sqrt{\frac{1}{2^n}}.
\]
